These are starting points, not guarantees of runtime. Air conditioners, electric water heaters, and induction cooktops can drain batteries quickly. The supplied RV comparison estimates that a 13,500 BTU roof air conditioner draws around 1,500 W while running, with startup surges above 3,000 W.

Don't forget the solar panels

A power station's maximum solar input is not the same as the wattage of the included panel bundle. The supplied results don't establish current bundled panel prices for every model, so confirm the exact package before purchasing.

For RV use, check:

Solar input: Make sure the station can accept the total wattage of your intended panels.

Panel compatibility: Confirm voltage and connector compatibility.

Battery capacity: A larger battery stores more energy but still needs enough sunlight to recharge.

RV connection: Verify whether you can power your intended RV loads through the available outlets or need compatible additional equipment.

My final recommendation

I'd choose the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 if your priority is powering a larger RV setup, including high-draw appliances. I'd choose the ALLPOWERS R4000 if you want a substantial battery and the reported discount, provided its weight and solar setup work for your RV.

One question would help me narrow this to the best complete station-and-panel package: Will you need to run your RV's roof air conditioner, or mainly the refrigerator, lights, and electronics?
